introduction.heading: Plumbing for Summit County homes
introduction.body:
Half of the homes in Summit County were built in 1995 or later, and about 21% before 1980, according to the U.S. Census Bureau. In newer homes like these, the first big plumbing jobs are often water heaters, fixtures and water softeners as the original equipment ages. A water heater usually lasts 10 to 15 years.

Water in Summit County comes from several systems. Park City runs its own, Summit Water serves areas including Jeremy Ranch and Kimball Junction from wells and a spring, and Mountain Regional Water brings Weber River water into the Snyderville Basin through its Lost Canyon project.

Summit County's building design criteria set a 36-inch frost line depth and a winter design temperature of -7°F.
